<thought>We need the number of aromatic carbons in the molecule. The only way to infer this without a structural description is to obtain the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample and count the signals that fall in the typical aromatic carbon chemical shift range (≈120–150 ppm). This will give the count of aromatic carbon environments, which corresponds to the number of aromatic carbons in the molecule (assuming no overlapping signals). We'll request the carbon NMR spectrum, then count the aromatic peaks.</thought>
